Worth a sentence: a shared primitive should take the floor as a parameter each consumer owns, not export one constant.

pairs.subject: retrieval
pairs.evidence: src-tauri/db/src/lib.rs:899 the FTS drift check counts kb_chunks_fts, an EXTERNAL-CONTENT table (:985 content='kb_chunks') whose full scan is answered by kb_chunks itself, so fts_count always equals chunk_count and the rebuild backfill at :907 can never fire - a never-indexed chunk stays invisible to the BM25 lane with no signal (reproduced: empty index gives COUNT=3, MATCH=0)

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/db/src/lib.rs:899 the drift check reads a view the source answers on the index's behalf - the technique's 'the check must read the index's own storage'; fix: count kb_chunks_fts_docsize or run the fts5 integrity-check command. Realized halves: :989 triggers couple FTS writes and deletes to kb_chunks in the same statement; src-tauri/db/src/vector_store.rs:163 delete_vectors_by_chunks takes the caller's connection so vector deletes can join the chunk-delete transaction
src-tauri/db/src/embedder.rs:50 model_name exposed for stamping; :107 a failed ONNX load is a named permanent-unavailable error, not a silent empty
src-tauri/db/src/vector_store.rs:132 sqlite-vec KNN returns identity-keyed (chunk_id, distance) rows via ORDER BY distance LIMIT - fewer rows when the index holds fewer than k, no positional lookup

pairs.registryProposal: Candidate application rust--chunking-and-indexing (SQLite FTS5): an external-content FTS5 table's COUNT(*) / full scan is served by the content table, so a source-vs-index count drift check over it is vacuous by construction. Count the <name>_docsize shadow table or use INSERT INTO t(t, rank) VALUES('integrity-check', 1). Reproducible in four lines of sqlite3; a concrete, stack-specific instance of 'the check must read the index's own storage'.
